summary: Two request flood events were recorded against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02, occurring while user-01 was logged on.

sequence.description: A request flood was initiated against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02.
A second request flood was recorded against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02.

findings.statement: Two distinct dos_flood events occurred against host-01 within a 6-minute window.

impact: host-01 was the target of the request floods, indicating it was the system under attack.
recommendations: Investigate the source IP ip-01 to determine if it is an internal or external address and check for other activity from this IP. Why: ip-01 is the source of both dos_flood events against host-01 (fx-025, fx-026).

Review the logs for host-01 during the time window 13:24:00Z to 13:30:00Z to assess the impact on services and check for any successful exploitation or data access. Why: The dos_flood events (fx-025, fx-026) targeted host-01, and the impact on its services is not detailed in the current events.
risk_justification: The risk score of 57 (medium) is consistent with a DoS attack that has been detected and is limited to two flood events, without evidence of data exfiltration or lateral movement.
uncertainty: It is not known whether user-01 is the attacker or a legitimate user whose session was coincident with the attack. (would be settled by: Authentication logs, user activity logs, and correlation with other events involving user-01.) The specific impact of the DoS flood on host-01's services (e.g., downtime, error rates) is not detailed. (would be settled by: System performance metrics, application logs, and service availability logs for host-01 during the incident window.) The relationship between the context event fx-024 (user-01 logging on to host-02) and the DoS events is unclear. (would be settled by: Network flow logs and host-02 activity logs to determine if host-02 was involved in the attack or if the login is unrelated.) Limitations: The evidence package contains only three events, two of which are the DoS floods. There is no data on the attack's origin, tools used, or post-attack activity. The context event fx-024 is not flagged and may be unrelated to the DoS attack, limiting the ability to draw a complete timeline of the incident.
